what_it_does: Ceph is a widely-used distributed storage system that stores data and metadata across a cluster of computers. Its main bottleneck is the messenger layer — the component that handles all network communication — which burns substantial CPU time on the host machines coordinating with other nodes, reducing the system's overall throughput and scalability. DoCeph solves this by moving the communication responsibility to a separate hardware accelerator called a Data Processing Unit (DPU), freeing the host CPU to focus on storage operations. The DPU handles incoming messages and transfers data using direct memory access (DMA), a technique that moves data between devices without involving the CPU. A pipelining technique ensures that while data is being transferred, buffer space is prepared in parallel, avoiding bottlenecks from fixed transfer sizes.
